01
PPP · Presentation

Notice the meaning

20 minutes
Lead-in 5 · Rule lab 15

Lead-in: What would you say?

Look at the four situations. Say one sentence for each picture. Use any modal verb you remember. There may be more than one good answer.

TRAVEL
At the airport: rules, documents, possibilities
HEALTH
At the doctor’s: advice and necessity
WORK
At work: responsibilities and ability
LIFE
Shopping: choices, advice, permission
Suggested elicitation: “You have a flight in two hours. What must / have to / can you do?” “Your friend feels ill. What should they do?” Accept imperfect answers now; the goal is diagnosis, not correction.
Strong obligation / prohibition

must

must + base verb
mustn’t + base verb
Must = very important / the speaker feels it is necessary.
I must finish this report tonight.
Mustn’t = it is prohibited. Do not do it.
You mustn’t smoke here.
Important: mustn’t does not mean “not necessary”. It means “not allowed”.
External necessity

have to

have / has to + base verb
don’t / doesn’t have to + base verb
Have to = a rule, schedule, situation or other person makes it necessary.
I have to wear an ID badge at work.
Don’t have to = no necessity. You can do it, but it is optional.
You don’t have to come early.
Past / future are easy: had to, will have to. “Must” does not have all tense forms.
Advice / recommendation

should

should + base verb
shouldn’t + base verb
Should = this is a good idea.
You should take a short break.
Shouldn’t = this is probably a bad idea.
You shouldn’t skip breakfast every day.
Advice is weaker than obligation: should < must / have to.
Ability / permission / possibility

can

can + base verb
can’t + base verb
Can = ability: “I can drive.” Permission: “You can leave early.”
Can’t = no ability or no permission: “I can’t swim.” / “You can’t park here.”
After can, never use “to”: can go, not “can to go”.

The difference that matters most

You mustn’t work tomorrow.
It is forbidden. You are not allowed to work.
You don’t have to work tomorrow.
It is optional. You can work, but it is not necessary.

Concept check

Teacher: Ask the student to explain the meaning after each answer: “Is it a rule, advice, permission, or no necessity?”
02
PPP · Controlled → freer practice

Choose, build, react

35 minutes
Pictures 10 · Sort 8 · Build 10 · Speed 7

Practice A · Picture detective

Choose the best sentence for each situation. Then explain why that modal fits the meaning.

Practice B · Meaning sorter

Select a sentence, then click the meaning it belongs to. Work fast: the goal is meaning, not translation.

0 / 10 correct

Practice C · Sentence workshop

Complete each sentence with the best modal form. Contractions are accepted.

Practice D · 60-second speed round

One question. Four choices. No overthinking.

TIME60
SCORE0
QUESTION0 / 10
Press “Start round” when you are ready.
Teacher: After the round, revisit only the mistakes. Ask the student to produce a new example with the same modal.

How to play

Choose a square.

A speaking challenge will appear here. Say a complete sentence with the target modal, then claim the square. Three in a row wins.

1 · ChoosePick any empty square.
2 · SpeakComplete the modal-verb challenge aloud.
3 · ClaimTake the square only after the sentence is complete.
Teacher game: both players answer. Computer game: the student answers; the computer makes its move automatically. Use “Show sample” only after speaking.
Production principle: Keep corrections delayed while the board is active. A square is earned for a clear, meaningful sentence — not for perfect pronunciation or every small grammar detail.

Quick reference

Modal cheat sheet

must / mustn’tStrong obligation / prohibition. “Mustn’t” = do not do it.
have to / don’t have toExternal necessity / no necessity. “Don’t have to” = optional.
should / shouldn’tAdvice: a good or bad idea.
can / can’tAbility, permission, or impossibility / no permission.
Formmust / should / can + base verb. No “to”. Have to is different: have/has to + base verb.
mustn’t ≠ don’t have to
Forbidden ≠ optional
